subject.title: fix: strip volatile output from exec result hash to fix no-progress detection (#93917)

question: Should repeated identical exec calls with the same nonzero exit metadata count as no progress even when their output changes?
rationale: The implementation fixes the reproduced runaway loop, but it can terminate retries whose only progress signal is changing nonzero output; that availability tradeoff requires maintainer intent rather than an automated code judgment.

options.title: Accept after live proof
options.body: Adopt the stable nonzero equivalence rule after an exact-head agent or gateway transcript demonstrates the intended breaker behavior and exit-zero control.

options.title: Preserve output-sensitive retries
options.body: Keep current ordinary-nonzero behavior and leave the reported exit-code-1 runaway loop unresolved until a richer progress classifier exists.

options.title: Design richer failure progress
options.body: Pause this PR and create an explicit distinction between meaningful nonzero-output progress and volatile failure noise.

recommendation.title: Accept after live proof
recommendation.body: Adopt the stable nonzero equivalence rule after an exact-head agent or gateway transcript demonstrates the intended breaker behavior and exit-zero control.
